comment: Divergences between the field tables, sdk-python and the docs JSON that a human has
looked at and accepted. tools/drift.py fails when this SET CHANGES - a new finding
that is not here, or an entry here that no longer fires - and never merely because it
is non-empty. A checker that is red on day one is a checker nobody reads by week two.
Every entry carries an owner and a reason. A type.conflict or a flag.conflict
additionally needs a resolution naming which input won: those two say the sources of
truth disagree about a type or about whether a field may be sent on a create, and
those are the findings an exemption must not be able to wave through.
sdk-python is pinned in tests/reference/sdk-python.sha and bumped by an explicit PR.

accepted.reason: Split is in this build only because an Invoice hydrates one out of its splits list. Its own verbs arrive with the rest of the bank surface; the table is complete so the nested hydration matches python byte for byte.
As verb.new:Split:get - Split's verbs are deferred, not missed.
As verb.new:Split:get - Split's verbs are deferred, not missed.

The docs list transactionIds as an Invoice filter and sdk-python's query() does not accept it. python is normative for the verb surface, and a filter no SDK has ever sent is not one this tier should be the first to prove against the API. Add the key when python does; -DSTARKBANK_LOOSE_QUERY sends it today.

The docs give event-attempt its own slug; sdk-python nests it as event/attempt. Both are right - the doc slug is a page and the python path is a package. sdk-c follows python and registers the resource EventAttempt, whose endpoint event/attempt core-c derives and the endpoint check confirms.
The docs slug is plural and sdk-python's package is institution. A naming divergence in the docs, not a missing resource.
The other half of resource.unjoined:institutions:python.

public-key is documented and has no sdk-python package: the key is fetched inside starkcore for signature verification, not modelled as a resource. sdk-c reaches it the same way, through starkbank_parse_and_verify.

sdk-python's request package is the raw escape hatch (get/post/patch/put/delete against any path), not an API resource, so the docs have no page for it. sdk-c has no equivalent yet; if one is added it is hand-written, never a table.

The docs tag Event.isDelivered STRING. sdk-python's Event carries a bool, its query() sends is_delivered through the api-cast that spells a bool True/False, and the recorded golden in tests/reference/slice.json shows isDelivered=False on the wire. The docs tag is the lossy input here.

sdk-python files external_id under '## Attributes (return-only)' and then accepts it as a Split.__init__ parameter, so api_json sends it on a create; the docstring's own wording for tags and scheduled ('default None', 'default now') is create-parameter language under the wrong heading. The table is right and python's prose is the bug. Split rides inside an Invoice's splits list in this slice, which is exactly where a caller sets these.

sdk-python contradicts itself: Transfer.__init__ takes account_type positionally with no default, while its docstring lists it under '## Parameters (optional)' with default 'checking'. The table follows the docstring and leaves REQUIRED off, because the API defaults it and refusing a create locally that the API would accept is the worse failure. Revisit if python ever makes the two halves agree.

sdk-python's DictKey.__init__ takes id=None under '## Parameters (optional)', but DictKey has no create() function at all - only get/query/page. The docstring section documents the constructor of a local convenience object, not an accepted create-payload key, because there is no create endpoint for a create-payload key to belong to. The table is right: id is RO, read through get()'s id argument like every other resource's id.
The other half of verb.new:Institution:query: sdk-c names the verb after the engine shape it actually uses (page) rather than manufacturing a same-named 'query' for a function that is not one.

sdk-python's institution.query() is itself rest.get_page(...)[0]: one page call, cursor discarded, no looping across pages - the PAGE shape wearing a different name. sdk-c exposes starkbank_institution_page directly instead of inventing an iterator python's own code never builds; pass NULL for out_cursor to match python's query() exactly.

sdk-python's create() is deprecated since v2.31.0 and unconditionally raises StarkError('deprecated'); it is a tombstone, not a working verb. Adding a create here would let a C caller do, over the wire, exactly what sdk-python refuses to do at all - so sdk-c has no create verb for Transaction and none is planned unless python's own create() starts working again.

sdk-python's Transaction.__init__ lists amount, description, external_id, receiver_id and tags under '## Parameters (required)'/'(optional)', but Transaction.create() is deprecated since v2.31.0 and unconditionally raises StarkError('deprecated') - there is no working create endpoint left for these to be sent to. The docstring describes the constructor signature that create() used to serialize before it was turned into a tombstone; the table follows the live behaviour and marks every field RO. See starkbank/transaction/transaction.h for the full reasoning, which covers all five conflicting fields.
As flag.conflict:Transaction:amount - create() is deprecated and always raises, so every '## Parameters' field is RO in the table regardless of the docstring's stale Parameters section.

picture is a real wire key sdk-python's update() sends, but it is never an attribute of the Workspace class - update() builds the value from two of its own parameters (picture, picture_type) and never stores either on the returned object. The table carries it as a PATCH-only field so the engine can validate a write to it; python simply has no field of that name to compare against.

The docs list names as a GET /v2/corporate-holder filter; sdk-python's holder.query()/page() accept no such keyword. python is normative for the verb surface, so the table does not add a filter no SDK sends.
As query.new:CorporateHolder:names - the docs' search filter has no counterpart in sdk-python's query()/page() keywords.

sdk-python's corporateholder.log.query()/page() accept ids and the docs' GET /v2/corporate-holder/log endpoint does not list it. python is normative for the verb surface, so the table keeps the filter python actually forwards to rest.get_stream/get_page even though the docs page omits it.

sdk-python spells the DELETE /v2/corporate-holder/:id call cancel(); sdk-c keeps every resource's DELETE_ID verb named starkbank_<resource>_delete for one consistent spelling across the whole SDK rather than a per-resource alias, the same choice sdk-c4 documents for Institution's page()/query() naming. The HTTP call is identical; only the C symbol's name differs from python's function name.
The other half of verb.new:CorporateHolder:cancel - sdk-c's starkbank_corporate_holder_delete is the same DELETE_ID call sdk-python names cancel(), not a verb sdk-python lacks.

parse_permissions is a module-level helper in corporateholder/__permission.py that turns a caller's raw list into Permission objects before CorporateHolder.__init__ stores it; it is not a REST verb and has no HTTP shape to give a table. drift.py's python reader collects every non-underscore module-level def as a candidate verb, which is what surfaces this one. Hydration and dehydration of a LIST_RESOURCE field is the engine's job in sdk-c, so nothing here is missing.

As verb.new:Permission:parse_permissions - corporaterule/__corporaterule.py's parse_rules is the same local-hydration helper, not a REST verb, and drift.py's python reader has no way to tell the two apart from a bare module-level def.

sdk-python's CorporateBalance.__init__ does 'self.updated = updated' with no check_datetime call at all, unlike every other resource's updated/created field - a bug of omission in sdk-python, not a documented STRING semantic: the class docstring's own example is a datetime.datetime, and CorporateBalance.get() hydrates the same ISO-8601 timestamp every other DATETIME field on the wire uses. The table follows the wire format and the docstring; python's missing coercion is the divergence.

pin is a real wire key sdk-python's update() sends, but it is never an attribute of the CorporateCard class - update() takes it as a bare keyword argument and stores it nowhere on the object. The table carries it as a PATCH-only field so the engine can validate a write to it; python simply has no field of that name to compare against. Same shape as sdk-c4's field.gone:Workspace:picture.

As verb.new:CorporateHolder:cancel - sdk-python spells DELETE /v2/corporate-card/:id cancel(); sdk-c keeps the uniform starkbank_corporate_card_delete spelling.

There is no python behaviour for the table to model, so - unlike CorporateHolder's and CorporateCard's query key lists - this one leaves expand out.

The class docstring's own example is a datetime.datetime and the wire carries the same ISO-8601 timestamp every other DATETIME field uses, so the table follows the wire format and python's missing coercion is the divergence.

verbEndpoint() has no way to learn a real path-parameter name for a named verb - every other named shape (CONTENT/CONTENT_INT/CONTENT_QUERY/SUB_RESOURCE) is spelled base + '/:id/' + verbName, and POST /v2/merchant-session/:uuid/purchase is the first docs endpoint to call that same slot ':uuid' instead of ':id'. This is the placeholder's name, not the route: the docs' own POST /v2/merchant-session, GET /v2/merchant-session/:id and GET /v2/dynamic-brcode/:uuid pair show ':uuid' and ':id' are used interchangeably across the docs for the same kind of slot (a server-assigned id in the path), never as two different parameters on one route. The method and the rest of the path (POST /v2/merchant-session/.../purchase) match exactly.
